instruction: Bouncing Cube Keyframes `scene.blend` contains a single unit-cube mesh object `Ball` located at the world origin with no animation data. The scene frame range is 1..240. keyframe a bouncing animation on `Ball.location.z` that depicts 10 bounces with diminishing height. Each successive peak must be 80% of the previous peak. Bounce schedule =============== - Base peak height: `H = 5.0 BU`. - Each bounce has a period of 24 frames (12 frames up + 12 frames down). - Impact frames (cube touches `z = 0`): frames 1, 25, 49, 73, 97, 121, 145, 169, 193, 217, 241 (11 keyframes). - Peak frames (cube at apex of each bounce): frames 13, 37, 61, 85, 109, 133, 157, 181, 205, 229 (10 keyframes). - Peak heights: the i-th peak (0-indexed, i = 0..9) has `z = H * 0.8**i`. - Bounce 1 apex (frame 13): z = 5.0000 - Bounce 2 apex (frame 37): z = 4.0000 - Bounce 3 apex (frame 61): z = 3.2000 - Bounce 4 apex (frame 85): z = 2.5600 - Bounce 5 apex (frame 109): z = 2.0480 - Bounce 6 apex (frame 133): z = 1.6384 - Bounce 7 apex (frame 157): z = 1.3107 - Bounce 8 apex (frame 181): z = 1.0486 - Bounce 9 apex (frame 205): z = 0.8389 - Bounce 10 apex (frame 229): z = 0.6711 Concretely, you must insert exactly 21 keyframes on `Ball.location.z` (`data_path='location'`, `array_index=2`) at the 11 impact frames (value 0) and the 10 peak frames (value `H * 0.8**i`). F-curve handles may use BEZIER interpolation. Only keyframe positions and values matter. Extend `scene.frame_end` to at least 241 so the full animation fits inside the scene range. Save the result as `answer.blend`. Requirements: =============== 1. A single mesh object named `Ball` exists at the world origin, is a unit cube (8 verts), and has no modifiers. 2. `Ball.animation_data.action` exists. 3. The action has an f-curve with `data_path='location'` and `array_index=2` containing exactly 21 keyframes. 4. The 21 keyframe frames exactly match {1, 13, 25, 37, 49, 61, 73, 85, 97, 109, 121, 133, 145, 157, 169, 181, 193, 205, 217, 229, 241}. 5. At each of the 11 impact frames, z = 0 (tol 1e-3). 6. At each of the 10 peak frames, z = H * 0.8**i (tol 1e-3). 7. `scene.frame_end >= 241`.
